harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca), signed node1's ed25519 host public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals node1, 10.100.43.10, 10y validity), and configured sshd via HostCertificate directive. Verified a client trusting only the CA's public key (via an @cert-authority known_hosts line, no pinned host key) connects successfully under StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, with sshd debug output showing 'matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'. Falsified by showing the same client fails with an empty known_hosts. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, triggered `shutdown -r now`, polled until SSH returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd active, the host certificate still served, and CA-trust-only connection still succeeding post-reboot. Cleaned up all temporary test artifacts (test known_hosts files, temporary SSH keypair, appended authorized_keys entry) added purely for verification.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 SSH config and host keys (OpenSSH 7.2p2 on Ubuntu 16)
Captured baseline: sshd active, listening on :22
Created SSH CA keypair /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca(.pub) via ssh-keygen
Signed node1's ed25519 host public key with the CA producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1 and 10.100.43.10, 3650-day validity
Backed up sshd_config and added 'HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub' directive
Validated config with sshd -t and restarted ssh service
Set up a temporary local SSH client trust test using @cert-authority known_hosts entry (no host key pinning) and confirmed successful StrictHostKeyChecking=yes connection
Verified via ssh -vvv debug output that the server presented the ed25519-cert and the client validated it via certificate, not a pinned key
Falsified by connecting with an empty known_hosts file and confirming failure (Host key verification failed)
Captured pre-restart boot_id from /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
Triggered a safe reboot via 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset, proving an actual restart
Re-verified post-restart: sshd active, host certificate file and sshd_config directive intact, and CA-trust-only client connection still succeeds
Cleaned up all temporary verification artifacts: known_hosts test files, temporary SSH keypair, and the appended authorized_keys line, leaving the pre-existing exec-access key untouched

evidence.requirement: SSH CA created on node1
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca(.pub)

evidence.requirement: Host key signed by the CA into a certificate
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub; ssh-keygen -L shows Signing CA, principals node1/10.100.43.10, validity

evidence.requirement: sshd configured to present the certificate
evidence.summary: Added HostCertificate directive to sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, restarted ssh service successfully

evidence.requirement: Client connects trusting only the CA, without pinning the host key
evidence.summary: SSH connection with only an @cert-authority known_hosts line (no pinned key) succeeded under StrictHostKeyChecking=yes; verbose log shows 'matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'

evidence.requirement: Falsification: connection fails without CA trust
evidence.summary: Same client with empty known_hosts fails strict host key checking, proving the CA trust line (not incidental config) enables the connection

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before restart
evidence.summary: sshd active and listening; baseline boot_id 9094f607-01ec-47c9-b0ff-db0b8c2a6d98 captured

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned REBOOT_TRIGGERED immediately

evidence.requirement: Node restart confirmed via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection refused during reboot, then new boot_id b6dd9b7c-9d4f-49d8-8745-96b0c7d4acac with fresh uptime after recovery, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service and certificate
evidence.summary: sshd active, HostCertificate directive and cert file intact post-reboot, and CA-trust-only client connection succeeds again after reboot

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of temporary verification artifacts
evidence.summary: Removed temporary known_hosts files, temporary SSH keypair, and appended authorized_keys entry, leaving pre-existing exec-access key untouched
